neighbours.label: Louisiana: New Orleans, Baton Rouge, Lafayette, Mardi Gras, Cajun and Creole food and the bayou; Mississippi, Alabama and Texas places in the same frames stay low
fire: Brass bands marched through the French Quarter of New Orleans.
Lawmakers in Baton Rouge passed the levee budget.
A Cajun cook in Lafayette stirred the gumbo for hours.
Kids on the parade route caught beads all through Mardi Gras.
Shrimp boats tie up along the bayou near Houma.
We ate beignets at a café near Jackson Square in New Orleans.
The swamp tour left Breaux Bridge before the heat set in.
Shreveport's casinos line the Red River.
quiet: Brass bands marched through the downtown streets of Memphis.
Lawmakers in Montgomery passed the road budget.
A cook in Biloxi stirred the seafood stew for hours.
Kids on the parade route caught candy all through the Fourth of July.
Shrimp boats tie up along the bay near Galveston.
We ate pancakes at a café near the courthouse square in Mobile.
The swamp tour left Fort Myers before the heat set in.
Tulsa's casinos line the Arkansas River.
